purpose: OF-01 reporting inventory only; not a source acquisition or publication feed. No missing holder is acquired by this file.
scope: Offices elected by all voters of a state/DC, including retention-election seats and elected statewide boards. Federal offices and district-only electorates are outside the statewide count. Normally elected seats remain included while their current holder was appointed to a vacancy.
counting: One expected seat per office membership, not per unique person. Court chief-justice roles chosen internally are included in the court seat total, not counted twice.
status: Source-list reporting inventory, checked against official state election, government, constitutional/statutory and court sources. It inventories office types and seat memberships, not verified current holders or completed reader coverage.

states.name: Arizona
states.scopeNote: The Lieutenant Governor office first takes office in January 2027; it is not a current seat on October 20, 2026. Corporation Commission has five statewide-elected seats. Court of Appeals retention electorates are regional, not statewide.

states.name: Colorado

offices.title: State Board of Education Member, At Large
University of Colorado Regent, At Large

states.scopeNote: Include only the one at-large State Board of Education seat and one at-large CU Regent; district seats are not statewide.

judicialExclusion.reason: State judges are appointed following Governor nomination and General Assembly approval; no statewide popular judicial ballot.

states.name: District Of Columbia

offices.title: State Board of Education Member, At Large

states.scopeNote: District-wide offices are the DC counterpart of statewide. Ward council/education/ANC seats are excluded. Shadow Senators and Representative are DC elected advocacy offices, distinct from the federal congressional Delegate.

judicialExclusion.reason: DC Court of Appeals and Superior Court judges are Presidentially nominated and Senate confirmed, not elected by DC voters.
State judges are appointed by the Governor with Senate confirmation, not popular statewide election.

offices.title: Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire

states.name: Hawaii
states.scopeNote: All nine OHA trustees are elected by the statewide electorate, including island-residency seats. Other executive department heads are appointed.

judicialExclusion.reason: Judges are initially appointed; retention is decided by the Judicial Selection Commission, not the statewide electorate.

states.name: Idaho
states.scopeNote: The fiscal office is State Controller, not State Auditor.

judicialExclusion.reason: Supreme Court and Appellate Court elections and retention use judicial districts, not the whole-state electorate.

states.name: Indiana

offices.title: Court of Appeals Judge, Districts 4 and 5

states.scopeNote: The constitutional Auditor of State office now uses State Comptroller. Court of Appeals Districts 1-3 retention is regional; Districts 4-5 retention is statewide (six seats). Tax Court judge has statewide retention.

judicialExclusion.reason: Supreme Court and Court of Appeals judges are elected by geographic judicial districts.

states.name: Louisiana
states.scopeNote: The current state executive list has seven elected officers. Superintendent of Education is appointed; Commissioner of Elections is no longer a separate elected office. PSC and BESE elected seats have district electorates.

judicialExclusion.reason: Supreme Court and lower appellate judges are elected by judicial districts.
State judges are appointed by the Governor with Governor Council approval, not popularly elected.

states.name: Maryland
states.scopeNote: Supreme Court retention is by appellate circuit. Appellate Court has seven circuit-based and eight at-large judges; only the eight at-large seats are counted here.

states.name: Maine
states.scopeNote: Only Governor is popularly elected statewide. Secretary, Treasurer, Attorney General and State Auditor are selected by the Legislature, so their current reader rows are preserved but do not increase the elected-seat target.

judicialExclusion.reason: State judges are appointed by the Governor and confirmed by the Senate, not popularly elected statewide.

states.name: Michigan
states.scopeNote: Four independently elected executive roles plus eight State Board members and three eight-member university boards elected statewide.

states.name: Minnesota
states.scopeNote: The State Treasurer office was abolished in 2003. The current constitution and current SOS filing page list five constitutional offices; an old legislature FAQ still lists Treasurer and is not used as authority.

judicialExclusion.reason: Supreme Court and Court of Appeals seats have district electorates.

states.name: Montana
states.scopeNote: State Auditor also serves as Commissioner of Securities and Insurance; count that one seat once. Supreme Court Clerk is a separately elected statewide office.

states.name: Nebraska
states.scopeNote: Public Service Commission, Education Board, Regents, six associate Supreme Court justices and six Court of Appeals judges have district electorates; only Chief Justice and the six Workers Compensation judges are counted as statewide judicial seats.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.scopeNote: Governor is the only statewide popular executive election. Executive Council members are elected by five separate districts. Secretary, Treasurer and judges are not popularly elected statewide.

judicialExclusion.reason: State judges are appointed by Governor and Executive Council, not popularly elected.

states.name: New Jersey
states.scopeNote: Governor and Lieutenant Governor are the only statewide popular executive offices. Attorney General and Secretary of State are appointed. A Lieutenant Governor who also serves as Secretary holds an additional appointed role, not another elected seat.

judicialExclusion.reason: State Supreme Court judges are appointed by Governor with Senate advice and consent.

states.name: New York
states.scopeNote: Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Comptroller and Attorney General are statewide popular offices; Court of Appeals is appointed and Supreme Court judges are elected by judicial district.

judicialExclusion.reason: Highest Court of Appeals is appointed; elected Supreme Court trial judges use judicial districts.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.scopeNote: All three appellate courts have statewide retention ballots, including the twelve Court of Civil Appeals seats; district residency for appointment does not make their retention electorate regional. Title 20 section 30.16 explicitly submits Civil Appeals retention to qualified electors of the state; this controls over an older state-library summary describing district retention.

offices.title: Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor and Industries

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.scopeNote: Secretary of the Commonwealth and Secretary of Education are appointed, not elected statewide. Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth courts are statewide electoral offices.

judicialExclusion.reason: Supreme Court appointments require Governor nomination and General Assembly approval, not public statewide election.

states.name: South Carolina
states.scopeNote: Adjutant General has been appointed since 2019; do not count it as an elected seat. Judges elected by the General Assembly are not statewide popular-election seats.

judicialExclusion.reason: General Assembly elects appellate judges; the public does not elect or retain them in statewide ballots.

offices.title: Commissioner of School and Public Lands

states.name: Tennessee
states.scopeNote: Governor is the sole statewide popularly elected executive office. Lieutenant Governor is elected by the Senate; Secretary, Comptroller and Treasurer are elected by the General Assembly. All appellate courts use statewide retention.

offices.title: Commissioner of General Land Office
aliases: Commissioner of the General Land Office

states.name: Utah
states.scopeNote: Supreme Court expanded from five to seven justices in 2026; Governor appointments and September oath report establish the two new seats. State Board of Education seats are district-elected.

states.name: Virginia
states.scopeNote: Judges selected by the General Assembly are not statewide popular-election seats.

judicialExclusion.reason: General Assembly selects state judges; the public does not elect them statewide.

states.name: Vermont
states.scopeNote: Supreme Court retention is decided by the General Assembly, not a statewide popular ballot.

judicialExclusion.reason: Supreme Court appointment and General Assembly retention are not statewide popular elections.

states.name: Wyoming
states.scopeNote: Include the single full-time Chancery Court judge, subject to statewide retention in November 2026, as well as five Supreme Court seats.

limitations: No current-holder acquisition was performed. A displayed title alone does not establish correct/current occupancy, an official holder source or contact. Counts include existing seats subject to future retention even if an incumbent was appointed. Official pages can retain obsolete summaries; current laws and current court organization take precedence. This file is READY gap evidence, never a runtime completeness gate.

sourceAudit.method: Read official office lists, constitutional/statutory provisions and court organization/election pages; current rules take precedence over obsolete summaries. Raw source responses and alternate web-reader evidence were retained with the production-copy task artifacts. Sources that failed one retrieval route were checked using alternate official sources or the web reader. No automated source-access outcome is used as a publication gate.
